git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Load project skills from the page and fire the model-arrived skill on every arrival

A project skill is a file on the Agent page, AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md:
frontmatter with its name and the trigger the app fires it on, then the text
the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection in one skills
message, which replaces file_report_instructions; the host keeps them by
trigger and refuses a bad payload with a bridge error, keeping the set it had.
Bridge version stays 1; the capability list gains project_skills. Project
turns the app starts before the skills arrive wait for them, as they wait for
the project instructions. The model never chooses a skill and there is no
tool to read one.

The first skill, model-opened-or-imported (trigger model_arrived), is the
former fileReportInstructions.ts text. It now fires on the request where a
load report first reaches the model: the turn the app starts when the person
opens or drops a file, and the continuation request after an object_import,
object_import_file or project_open call whose result carries a report. It goes
in as that request's last item, after a picture of the active plate (the
offscreen iso render view_render uses, drawn when the request is built and
only when the plate has a printable object). Neither is stored in the
conversation, and OpenAIResponsesAgent leaves both out of the history it builds
the turn's next request from. When the conversation has no setup title and no
answered intent field, the host appends one fixed sentence saying nothing is
recorded about what the print is for. The text now covers both ways a model
arrives, says what the picture is, and drops three sentences; it is 6,525
bytes, from 6,635, and 6,624 with the host's sentence.

A project_open run by the model replaces the conversation's document and ends
the turn, so its result reaches no model; a test holds that in place.

view_render's description also offers the picture for telling what an object
is when its name does not say; project_tools.json is regenerated.
EOF

# The "model arrived" skill: report

Branch `claude/skill-model-arrived`, two commits on local `jusprin-newui` 86f8395071 (not pushed, not merged):
bb148b0b9f (app and its tests) and 0f9ba01d33 (prompt eval). 86f8395071 replaced 46ee617812 on `jusprin-newui` this morning and contains its changes.

## 1. Problem

The project chat's guidance for "a model just arrived" (`fileReportInstructions.ts`) reached the model only when the person opened or dropped a file. When the model itself imported a model with a tool, the reply carried the same OrcaSlicer load report with no guidance, so the model read the dialog answers and the file's notes with nothing telling it how to treat them. There was also no general way for the app to add situational text ("skills") to a request. Three more skills are planned and need one.

## 2. What changed

**The loader.** Each skill is a file on the Agent page: `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Its frontmatter has `name` and `trigger`, and the body is the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection in one `skills` bridge message; this replaces `file_report_instructions`. The host stores the skills by trigger and knows nothing about how many there are. It refuses a bad payload with a bridge error and keeps the set it already had. The rules: one message, names sorted, one skill per trigger, at most 16 KiB of text per skill, at most 256 KiB in total. Project turns that the app starts before the skills arrive wait for them, the same way they wait for the project instructions. The bridge version stays 1, and the capability list gains `project_skills`. Nothing was ported from the old loader's model-picks-a-skill design: no `skill_read` tool, no skill index and no prompt text about choosing.

**The first skill.** `model-opened-or-imported` (trigger `model_arrived`) is the old file-open text, moved. The host adds it to the request where a load report first reaches the model:
- when the person opens or drops a file, on the request that starts the reply;
- when the model calls `object_import` (or `object_import_file`, or a `project_open` that fails), on the next request, after the tool results.

The skill is always the request's last item, with a picture of the active plate just before it. The picture is the offscreen iso render that `view_render` uses. It is drawn when the request is built, and only when the plate has a printable object. Neither the skill nor the picture is stored in the conversation. Neither appears on any later request, including the next request of the same turn.

**Changes to the text.**
- The opening sentence ("They have asked for nothing yet…") is rewritten so it covers both the person's open and a tool's import.
- One sentence now says what the picture is.
- Three sentences are gone: the `uiLanguage` sentence (a later sentence covers it), the "left column" sentence, and a duplicate of the tiny-model instruction already in the table.
- Size: the old text was 6,635 bytes; the new text is 6,525 bytes, or 6,624 bytes when the host's sentence is added.

**Where each piece of text lives.** All the model-read text is on the page (the skill). C++ supplies only state-based parts:
- the picture;
- the decision to fire the skill;
- one fixed sentence, added when the chat has no setup title and no answered intent field: "Nothing is recorded about what this print is for; once it is known, check the presets against it."

**Other changes.**
- `view_render`'s description now also offers the picture "to tell what an object is when its name does not say". `project_tools.json` was regenerated.
- The reminder line on later requests is unchanged.

**Lines changed.** App code: +376/−69. Tests and eval: +914/−76. The re-recorded `requests.json`: +9,349/−2,169.

## 3. Tests and results

All tests were run on the final build:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 303 cases pass, 12 of them new or extended |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest, after `jusprin_web` was rebuilt | 421 tests pass |
| Shell harness, default scenario | 553 checks, 0 failures |
| `test_steps.py` | 15 tests pass |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 19 cases render |

The new tests cover:
- the skill on the person's open, on `object_import` and on `object_import_file`, and on no later request;
- the picture, both present and absent;
- the purpose sentence, both present and absent, including an intent question that has no answer yet;
- refusal of a bad payload (14 kinds);
- the wait for the skills;
- the adapter dropping the skill and picture from the next request;
- the parser.

I checked that every new test fails when its behaviour is removed. I broke each behaviour on purpose in two C++ rounds, plus once in the parser and once in the runner, saw the matching tests fail, and restored the code.

**The eval.** `requests.json` was re-recorded with 0 failures. The 17 old points are identical apart from ids, timestamps and temporary paths. Two cases are new:
- `model-opened-unnamed`: the person imports `scan_0417.drc` (the Stanford bunny).
- `model-imported-by-tool`: the person attaches `part_7.drc` (the calicat), and `object_import` adds it.

The recorder checks that the skill and the picture are on exactly those two requests and absent from the next one. It saved both pictures, and I looked at them: they show the bunny and the cat.

## 4. Remaining issues

- **A `project_open` called by the model ends the turn.** Opening a project replaces the chat's document, which cancels the turn, so the result never reaches a model and the opened project's chat says nothing. I confirmed this in the real app: no request followed for two minutes. A test now holds this behaviour in place. Fixing it is your call. My recommendation: post the load report as a note in the opened project's chat and start a turn there, the same way a person's open works today.
- **The eval model cannot see pictures.** OpenRouter lists `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as text only, and the app's default is `gpt-5.4-mini`. The two new cases may fail with a request error, or run without the picture.
- **The import picture hides one object.** `object_import` put the cat on top of the box (`object_analyze` reports them as overlapping), so the picture shows only the cat. That is how the import places objects today. The case does not ask the reply to mention the overlap.
- **Retrying a failed request after an import does not re-send the skill.**

**Proposed batch, not run.** The two new cases, 3 runs each: about 18 requests, roughly 200k–250k input tokens and 6 judge calls. Start with 1 run of each, to see whether OpenRouter accepts the picture for this model. If it refuses, choose between dropping the picture in the runner and running these two cases on an image model such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Optionally, run all 19 cases × 3 (about 950k input tokens) to check the `view_render` description change.

Mostly, yes. Here is what I'll build, then four questions where your answer changes the code, and one decision still pending from before.

**The skills mechanism**
- **Two kinds of skill, one loader.** Every skill stays a `SKILL.md` on the page.
  - An event skill has a `trigger`, and the app injects it when that event happens. The model-arrived skill is one.
  - A discretionary skill has a `description`, and the model can read it whenever it judges it useful.
- **`skill_read` is ported.** It returns a skill's text by name. Paired with a list of skill names and descriptions, it works the way other harnesses (Claude Code, Agent Skills) do.
- **This reverses part of the original brief.** It said "do not port `skill_read`" and "the model never chooses." Event skills still never depend on the model choosing. The model only chooses among the discretionary ones.

**`project_open` called by the AI**
1. The current turn is interrupted. That already happens when the project is swapped.
2. Opening an internal project does nothing.
3. Otherwise, the events and dialogs OrcaSlicer produces during the open are gathered by the existing load-report collection in the workspace adapter. The same collector already gathers them for the AI's open, so I'll move code rather than write new.
4. The collected report is handed to the opened project's new chat, through exactly the path your own opens take today: the file note, then a turn with the model-arrived skill.
5. One mechanism, nothing kept alongside. I read "the hard-coded one-off" as the old special-cased file-report instructions, which are already gone. I'll also check what else in that path is still special-cased (see question 4).

**Changes to the skill text**
- Check the available presets and the selected ones, and suggest a change if the selected ones look wrong for this model.
- Ask the person whether the AI should look at the model to guess what it's for, the intent, and the slicing strategy.

**Questions**
1. **The picture.** Today the plate picture is attached to the model automatically. "Ask whether to look at the model" suggests no picture until the person says yes, after which the AI calls `view_render`. Should I remove the automatic picture? I recommend removing it. Otherwise the question asks permission for something the model has already seen.
2. **Internal project.** Today a reopened project with its own conversation is skipped, but it is still greeted if OrcaSlicer said something while loading it, such as a dialog. Should internal projects stay silent even then? I recommend keeping today's exception, since that dialog may matter.
3. **Discretionary skills.** None exist yet. Should this task ship only the mechanism, with no discretionary skill? Or should it also include some? If so, which ones? Without one, the tool would be offered with nothing to read, so I'd offer `skill_read` and its list only when at least one discretionary skill exists. Where should that list go?
   - In `skill_read`'s description (my recommendation): the standing prompt stays principles-only.
   - In the system prompt, as Claude Code does.
4. **What else becomes a skill.** The app adds two pieces of text itself:
   - the reminder line on later requests ("Earlier file-load reports… are source data");
   - the fixed "Nothing is recorded about what this print is for" sentence.

   Once the skill checks presets, that sentence mostly repeats it, so I'd delete it. Should the reminder line also move into a skill? The original brief said to keep it as it is.

**Limits the new text runs into.** The skill currently says to end with one question or offer and to stay under 90 words. The presets suggestion plus the "may I look?" question push against both. I'll have it lead with whichever matters more and allow the second. The text will also grow, so the original "delete at least as much as you add" rule no longer holds.

**Still pending:** the eval model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, reads text only. If you drop the automatic picture (question 1), that problem mostly goes away.

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

- [jusprin-v2-poc rebase, not merge](jusprin-v2-poc-rebase-not-merge.md) — branch forks from release/v2.4; rebase only the fork's commits (2 conflicts) instead of merging upstream in (531).
- [Verify before claiming rebase risk](fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming.md) — three checks that would have caught three wrong confident claims in a fork audit.
- [Phase 1 shell wraps the intact Notebook](jusprin-shell-phase-1-design.md) — hide the tab strip, don't reparent Plater; sidebar policy seam; evidence doc location.
- [Inherited teardown crash](orca-inherited-teardown-crash.md) — exiting with volumes loaded segfaults in ~GLCanvas3D via destroyed Plater priv; predates the shell.
- [Worktree build recipe](jusprin-worktree-build.md) — cmake configure line reusing existing deps; use /Applications/CMake.app cmake, not Homebrew's; BUILD_TESTS=ON for tests; build jusprin_web explicitly after page edits or live runs use a stale prompt.

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.

- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.

A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux

- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.

- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the model that just arrived, opened by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture. From it and the report, make an educated guess at what the object is, what it is likely for, and how it should be sliced (orientation, supports, strength), and say it as a guess. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against that guess, against the printers the person has set up, and against the presets available (presets_list); when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it.

Write one useful message for someone new to 3D printing. Lead with the most consequential unresolved issue. Explain what it means for this print in everyday language. Briefly explain an unfamiliar term when the person needs it to understand the consequence. Explain where a warning came from when the report shows it: what the file contains, what I noticed while loading it, whether its settings were applied, and what still needs checking. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. When nothing in the report needs attention, say so in a few words. Do not recite routine loading details, every notice, or file metadata. Include dimensions only when they affect the issue. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed. End with your best guess at what the person wants to do next, in whatever form fits: a question, an offer or a suggested step, not a menu of alternatives.
Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.

Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short.

Speak about a project the Agent opens in its own chat, and add skill_read

A project_open the in-app Agent runs replaces the conversation with the
opened project's, which ends the turn that asked, so the call's result and
its load report reached no model and the opened project's chat said nothing.

opened project's chat on the next timer tick, once the project boundary has
settled, through the same on_file_loaded path a file the person opens takes:
the file note, then a turn with the model-arrived skill and the plate's
picture. The existing rule still holds: a reopened project with its own
conversation is greeted only when OrcaSlicer said something while loading it,
and continuing an earlier project loads nothing and says nothing. An MCP
client's project_open is left alone.

may read on its own. A skill may now have a description beside or instead of
a trigger; skill_read is offered only while at least one skill has one, lists
them in its own description, and reads only those. None exists yet, so no
request carries the tool today.

The model-arrived skill now tells the model to look at the attached picture
and guess what the object is, what it is for and how to slice it, to check
the selected presets and plate type against that guess and the presets
available and suggest a better one without changing it, and to end with its
best guess at what the person wants next in whatever form fits, instead of
one question or offer in under 90 words. It is 6,918 bytes.
EOF

# The "model arrived" skill: report

The branch is `claude/skill-model-arrived`. It has four commits on top of local `jusprin-newui` 86f8395071 and is neither pushed nor merged:
- bb148b0b9f – the skill loader and the skill, with their tests
- 0f9ba01d33 – the prompt eval cases and a new recording
- 5d790d603f – the project_open hand-off, `skill_read`, and the revised skill text
- 0094812092 – the project_open eval case and a new recording

86f8395071 replaced 46ee617812 on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-10-17, and contains its changes.

## 1. Problem

The project chat had one piece of situational guidance: what to say when a model arrives. It reached the model only when the person opened or dropped a file. It did not reach the model in two cases:
- **The AI imports a model** in the middle of a turn. The tool's reply carried OrcaSlicer's load report, but no guidance.
- **The AI opens a model with `project_open`.** Opening a project replaces the chat's document with the new project's, which ends the turn. The report reached no model, and the opened project's chat said nothing at all.

There was also no general way for the app to add situational text, called "skills", to a request.

## 2. What changed

**Skills on the page.** Each skill is a file on the Agent page: `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The frontmatter (the header at the top of the file) holds the skill's `name`, plus a `trigger`, a `description`, or both. The body is the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection in one `skills` bridge message, which replaces `file_report_instructions`.

The app refuses a bad message with a bridge error and keeps the skills it already had. The rules are:
- names sorted, at most one skill per trigger;
- each description one line of at most 300 bytes;
- each skill's text at most 16 KiB, and at most 256 KiB for the whole message.

The bridge version stays 1; the capability list gains `project_skills`. A project turn that the app starts before the skills arrive waits for them.

**Two kinds of skill.**
- **A skill with a trigger belongs to the app.** When its event happens, the app adds the skill as the last item of the one request where the model first reads about that event. It is never stored in the conversation, and it appears on no later request, including the next request of the same turn.
- **A skill with a description belongs to the model.** The model reads it with `skill_read`, which is ported from the suspended skills branch. `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own tool description and reads only those. It is offered only while at least one such skill exists. None exists yet, so no request carries `skill_read` today.

**The first skill.** `model-opened-or-imported` (trigger `model_arrived`) is the old file-open text, moved into a skill file. It goes out with a picture of the active plate placed just before it. The picture is the offscreen iso view that `view_render` uses, drawn when the request is built. It fires in four situations:

| What happened | Where the skill goes |
|---|---|
| The person opens or drops a file | On the request that starts the reply |
| The AI runs `object_import`, or a `project_open` that fails | After the tool results, in the same turn |
| The AI's `project_open` succeeds | In the opened project's chat: the app posts the load report there and starts a turn, the same path the person's own open takes |
| An MCP client opens or imports anything | Never |

When an existing project is reopened with its conversation, the app speaks only if OrcaSlicer said something while loading it, as before. When the AI continues an earlier project, nothing is loaded, so nothing is said.

**Skill text.** The skill now tells the model to:
- look at the attached picture and guess what the object is, what it is for, and how to slice it;
- check the selected presets and plate type against that guess and against the available presets, and suggest a better one without changing it;
- end with its best guess at what the person wants next, in whatever form fits.

The old "one question or offer, under 90 words" rule is gone. The text grew from 6,635 to 6,918 bytes.

**Where the text lives.** Everything the model reads is on the page. C++ supplies only things built from the app's state:
- the picture;
- the decision to fire a skill;
- the list of skill names and descriptions in `skill_read`'s description;
- one fixed sentence when no purpose is recorded for the print.

**Also changed.**
- `view_render`'s description now also says it can tell what an object is.
- `project_tools.json` was regenerated.

**Size.** App code: +507/−83 lines. Tests and eval: +1,164/−77 lines. `requests.json`: +11,952/−2,169 lines.

## 3. Tests and results

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 310 cases pass |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest, after `jusprin_web` was rebuilt | 421 tests pass |
| Shell harness, default scenario | 0 failures |
| `test_steps.py` | 15 tests pass |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 20 cases render |

The new tests cover:
- the three ways a model can arrive inside the app: your own open, the AI's import, and the AI's open;
- MCP opens, which stay silent;
- continuing an earlier project;
- the skill and picture appearing on no later request;
- the picture and the purpose sentence, each both present and absent;
- `skill_read`: when it is offered, what it may read, and its arguments;
- bad skills messages being refused;
- the parser.

I broke each behaviour on purpose and saw its test fail.

**Real app.** The AI's `project_open` now produces a request in the opened project's chat. That request holds only the report, the picture and the skill, with none of the old chat's history. The picture shows the opened model.

**Eval recording.** `requests.json` was recorded again with 0 failures. Only the skill text changed on the earlier points; other differences are ids, timestamps and temporary paths. There are three skill cases: `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`. The recorder checks that the skill and picture sit on exactly the right request and are gone from the next one.

## 4. Remaining issues

- **No live batch was run** (you'll test it). The eval model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, is listed by OpenRouter as text-only, so it may refuse the picture or run without it.
- **The original brief named `object_import_file`, which the in-app chat cannot call.** It is offered only to MCP clients. The eval case uses `object_import` instead, which imports a file the person attached to their message.
- **`object_import` placed the cat on top of the existing box,** so the picture hides the box. That is how imports are placed today; this change didn't cause it.
- **Two small effects of the AI's `project_open`:**
  - The person's request ("open part_9.drc") stays in the old project's chat.
  - Retrying a failed request after an import does not re-send the skill.

# The "model arrived" skill: report

Branch `claude/skill-model-arrived`, two commits on local `jusprin-newui` 86f8395071 (not pushed, not merged):
bb148b0b9f (app and its tests) and 0f9ba01d33 (prompt eval). 86f8395071 replaced 46ee617812 on `jusprin-newui` this morning and contains its changes.

## 1. Problem

The project chat's guidance for "a model just arrived" (`fileReportInstructions.ts`) reached the model only when the person opened or dropped a file. When the model itself imported a model with a tool, the reply carried the same OrcaSlicer load report with no guidance, so the model read the dialog answers and the file's notes with nothing telling it how to treat them. There was also no general way for the app to add situational text ("skills") to a request. Three more skills are planned and need one.

## 2. What changed

**The loader.** Each skill is a file on the Agent page: `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Its frontmatter has `name` and `trigger`, and the body is the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection in one `skills` bridge message; this replaces `file_report_instructions`. The host stores the skills by trigger and knows nothing about how many there are. It refuses a bad payload with a bridge error and keeps the set it already had. The rules: one message, names sorted, one skill per trigger, at most 16 KiB of text per skill, at most 256 KiB in total. Project turns that the app starts before the skills arrive wait for them, the same way they wait for the project instructions. The bridge version stays 1, and the capability list gains `project_skills`. Nothing was ported from the old loader's model-picks-a-skill design: no `skill_read` tool, no skill index and no prompt text about choosing.

**The first skill.** `model-opened-or-imported` (trigger `model_arrived`) is the old file-open text, moved. The host adds it to the request where a load report first reaches the model:
- when the person opens or drops a file, on the request that starts the reply;
- when the model calls `object_import` (or `object_import_file`, or a `project_open` that fails), on the next request, after the tool results.

The skill is always the request's last item, with a picture of the active plate just before it. The picture is the offscreen iso render that `view_render` uses. It is drawn when the request is built, and only when the plate has a printable object. Neither the skill nor the picture is stored in the conversation. Neither appears on any later request, including the next request of the same turn.

**Changes to the text.**
- The opening sentence ("They have asked for nothing yet…") is rewritten so it covers both the person's open and a tool's import.
- One sentence now says what the picture is.
- Three sentences are gone: the `uiLanguage` sentence (a later sentence covers it), the "left column" sentence, and a duplicate of the tiny-model instruction already in the table.
- Size: the old text was 6,635 bytes; the new text is 6,525 bytes, or 6,624 bytes when the host's sentence is added.

**Where each piece of text lives.** All the model-read text is on the page (the skill). C++ supplies only state-based parts:
- the picture;
- the decision to fire the skill;
- one fixed sentence, added when the chat has no setup title and no answered intent field: "Nothing is recorded about what this print is for; once it is known, check the presets against it."

**Other changes.**
- `view_render`'s description now also offers the picture "to tell what an object is when its name does not say". `project_tools.json` was regenerated.
- The reminder line on later requests is unchanged.

**Lines changed.** App code: +376/−69. Tests and eval: +914/−76. The re-recorded `requests.json`: +9,349/−2,169.

## 3. Tests and results

All tests were run on the final build:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 303 cases pass, 12 of them new or extended |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest, after `jusprin_web` was rebuilt | 421 tests pass |
| Shell harness, default scenario | 553 checks, 0 failures |
| `test_steps.py` | 15 tests pass |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 19 cases render |

The new tests cover:
- the skill on the person's open, on `object_import` and on `object_import_file`, and on no later request;
- the picture, both present and absent;
- the purpose sentence, both present and absent, including an intent question that has no answer yet;
- refusal of a bad payload (14 kinds);
- the wait for the skills;
- the adapter dropping the skill and picture from the next request;
- the parser.

I checked that every new test fails when its behaviour is removed. I broke each behaviour on purpose in two C++ rounds, plus once in the parser and once in the runner, saw the matching tests fail, and restored the code.

**The eval.** `requests.json` was re-recorded with 0 failures. The 17 old points are identical apart from ids, timestamps and temporary paths. Two cases are new:
- `model-opened-unnamed`: the person imports `scan_0417.drc` (the Stanford bunny).
- `model-imported-by-tool`: the person attaches `part_7.drc` (the calicat), and `object_import` adds it.

The recorder checks that the skill and the picture are on exactly those two requests and absent from the next one. It saved both pictures, and I looked at them: they show the bunny and the cat.

## 4. Remaining issues

- **A `project_open` called by the model ends the turn.** Opening a project replaces the chat's document, which cancels the turn, so the result never reaches a model and the opened project's chat says nothing. I confirmed this in the real app: no request followed for two minutes. A test now holds this behaviour in place. Fixing it is your call. My recommendation: post the load report as a note in the opened project's chat and start a turn there, the same way a person's open works today.
- **The eval model cannot see pictures.** OpenRouter lists `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as text only, and the app's default is `gpt-5.4-mini`. The two new cases may fail with a request error, or run without the picture.
- **The import picture hides one object.** `object_import` put the cat on top of the box (`object_analyze` reports them as overlapping), so the picture shows only the cat. That is how the import places objects today. The case does not ask the reply to mention the overlap.
- **Retrying a failed request after an import does not re-send the skill.**

**Proposed batch, not run.** The two new cases, 3 runs each: about 18 requests, roughly 200k–250k input tokens and 6 judge calls. Start with 1 run of each, to see whether OpenRouter accepts the picture for this model. If it refuses, choose between dropping the picture in the runner and running these two cases on an image model such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Optionally, run all 19 cases × 3 (about 950k input tokens) to check the `view_render` description change.

The skill now fires every time a model arrives in the in-app chat, including when the AI opens a model file as a new project; MCP clients still trigger nothing. `skill_read` is ported, and the skill text has the changes you asked for. All of this is on `claude/skill-model-arrived` as two more commits (5d790d603f, 0094812092), not pushed or merged.

**What happens when the AI calls `project_open`**
1. The turn that asked is interrupted, because opening a project swaps in the new project's chat.
2. The report OrcaSlicer collected while loading goes to the opened project's chat, after the swap has settled. That is the same path your own open uses: the file note, then a turn with the skill and the plate picture.
3. Reopening an existing project with its conversation behaves as before: the AI speaks only if OrcaSlicer said something while loading. When the AI continues an earlier project, nothing loads, so nothing is said.

I checked this in the real app. The first request in the opened project's chat holds only the report, the picture and the skill, with none of the old chat's history, and the picture shows the opened model.

**What fires the skill now:**
- your own open or drop;
- the AI's `object_import`, or a `project_open` that fails (in the same turn, after the tool results);
- the AI's `project_open` that succeeds (in the opened project's chat).

**`skill_read`**
- A skill can now have a `trigger` (the app adds it when that event happens), a `description` (the model can read it with `skill_read`), or both.
- `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own tool description and reads only those.
- It is offered only while at least one described skill exists. None exists, so no request carries `skill_read` today.

**Skill text changes**
- It tells the model to look at the attached picture and guess what the object is, what it's for and how to slice it.
- It checks the selected presets and plate type against that guess and the available presets, and suggests a better one without changing anything.
- It ends with the model's best guess at what you want next, in whatever form fits. The "one question or offer, under 90 words" rule is gone.
- The text grew from 6,635 to 6,918 bytes.

**Tests**
- Everything passes: the bridge tests (310), `workspace_contract_tests` (42), the AgentUI tests (421), the shell harness default scenario (0 failures), the offline eval-runner tests (15), and render-only on all 20 cases.
- I broke each new behaviour on purpose and saw its test fail. The `skill_read` argument check had no test then, so I added one.
- `requests.json` was re-recorded with 0 failures, and it now has a third skill case, `model-opened-by-tool`. On the other points only the skill text changed, apart from ids and timestamps.

**Two things you'll notice**
- When the AI opens a model as a new project, your request ("open part_9.drc") stays in the old project's chat. The AI's first message about the file appears in the new project's chat.
- The live eval hasn't been run, as you said you'd do it. OpenRouter lists DeepSeek V4 Flash as text-only, so it may refuse the plate picture.

The report is updated at [skill-model-arrived-report.md](skill-model-arrived-report.md), untracked.

content.text:
The new skill keeps most of the old text. One paragraph is new, a few sentences were reworded or removed, and the notice table is untouched. Old text: `fileReportInstructions.ts` at 86f8395071. New text: the body of `skills/model-opened-or-imported/SKILL.md`.

**Title**
- Old: "# The first message after opening a file"
- New: "# The first message after a model arrives"

**Opening paragraph**
- Old: "For this one response, write the first message about the file the person just opened. They have asked for nothing yet, so this message reports and offers, from the report alone."
- New: "For this one response, write the first message about the model that just arrived, opened by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for."
- Why: the old wording only held when the person opened a file, not when the AI imported one at the person's request.

**Sources paragraph** (last sentence replaced)
- Removed: "uiLanguage is the app's interface language, supplied even when there are no notices." The closing "Write in uiLanguage" line still covers it.
- Added: "The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view."

**New paragraph** (inserted before "Write one useful message…")
> Look at the attached picture when there is one. From it and the report, make an educated guess at what the object is, what it is likely for, and how it should be sliced (orientation, supports, strength), and say it as a guess. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against that guess, against the printers the person has set up, and against the presets available (presets_list); when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it.

**"Write one useful message…" paragraph**
- Removed: "When an issue remains, end with one specific next step I can help with, phrased as one question or offer; do not give a menu of alternatives."
- Old: "When nothing needs attention, acknowledge that the model loaded in one sentence."
- New: "When nothing in the report needs attention, say so in a few words."
- Added at the end: "End with your best guess at what the person wants to do next, in whatever form fits: a question, an offer or a suggested step, not a menu of alternatives."

**Notice guide intro**
- Removed: "The notice guide below is for *you* to read. Its left column gives examples of wording you may encounter, not identifiers assigned by app code."
- Old: "The guidance is deliberately not a code classification table."
- New: "The guide below is deliberately not a code classification table."

**Paragraph after the table**
- Removed: "If a tiny model was left unscaled, give its final size and ask the intended size." The table's "Object too small" row already says this.

**Last line**
- Old: "Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Usually stay under 90 words. When no action is needed, stop without a question."
- New: "Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short."

**Added by the app, not in the file**
When the chat has no setup title and no answered intent field, the app adds one sentence, written in C++, after a blank line: "Nothing is recorded about what this print is for; once it is known, check the presets against it."

**Size:** 6,635 bytes before, 6,918 after, plus 99 bytes when the app adds its sentence.

+The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
+| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
+| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |

+| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
